newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $12.576 bln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $12.576 bln.

text.p: Venezuela's total foreign reserves rose $351 million, or 2.9 percent, to $12.576 billion on September 23, according to new figures released by the central bank.
Reserves were up from a revised $12.225 billion on September 13, the bank's latest weekly bulletin of indicators showed.
Under a new reporting format, the bank also reported daily foreign reserve levels from Friday September 17 through to Monday September 23. Reserves on Friday September 20 stood at $12.510 billion.

Government officials have said they expect foreign reserves to grow by $1.5 billion over the course of 1996. From reserve levels of $9.702 billion on April 19 -- the last working day before exchange controls were lifted on April 22 -- reserves now stand up $2.874 billion, or 30 percent.
From the start of the year they now stand up $2.863 billion, or 29 percent.
Venezuela's total foreign reserves fell $1.784 billion, or 15.5 percent, in 1995 to end the year at $9.723 billion, the figures showed.
